chunks: Safwan narrated from Ibn Muskān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
‘Alī (peace be upon him) disliked exchanging two wasqs of the dates of Medina for one wasq of the dates of Khaybar.

key_terms.تَمْرِ الْمَدِينَةِ: dates of Medina (known for high quality)
key_terms.تَمْرِ خَيْبَرَ: dates of Khaybar (a specific regional variety)
key_terms.وَسْقَيْنِ: two wasqs (a unit of volume/weight for dry goods)
key_terms.يَكْرَهُ: disliked (expressing legal preference or dislike, not prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali dislike regarding the exchange of dates from Medina and Khaybar?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the practical application of *karāhah* (dislike/preference) in commercial transactions, specifically regarding the exchange of dates of differing qualities and origins. It reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential emphasis on fairness and transparency in barter (*mubādah*), ensuring that subtle disparities in quality or market value do not lead to hidden inequity between parties.
